before.title: 2025-2026 CX-70 Low 12V Battery or No-Start - Test Before Replacing
before.description: A low lead-acid-battery warning, no-start condition, or cluster full of low-voltage messages can occur after the 12V battery has discharged, but the symptom alone does not prove a defective battery or a software-related parked draw. Mazda specifies different test inputs for the CX-70 powertrains: the Inline-6 uses a 75D23L lead-acid battery rated at 465 CCA, while the PHEV uses a Q85 battery rated at 520 CCA and 65 Ah. Mazda also identifies storage, repeated power-on use without activating the drive system, loose or corroded connections, charging-system faults, accessories, excessive key-off draw, and an aged battery as distinct possibilities.
before.solution: Start with the exact powertrain and battery label, then inspect the case, hold-down, terminals, grounds, state of charge, and charging system. Have the battery fully charged and tested with Mazda's specified procedure; a GOOD result returns it to service, CHARGE AND RETEST requires charging and retesting, and replacement follows only a confirmed REPLACE result or the bulletin's repeat-failure path. If a fully charged, serviceable battery discharges again, measure key-off parasitic draw using Mazda's sleep-state procedure and isolate the circuit, module, accessory, or connection responsible. Do not order PE1X-18-520A, a Group 35 AGM, or a maintainer from this symptom alone; confirm the installed specification, powertrain, test result, and diagnosed cause first.
symptoms: Low lead-acid or 12V battery warning
Vehicle will not enter READY or start after sitting
Multiple low-voltage messages after a discharged battery
Battery requires repeated recharging
affectedSystems: M Hybrid Boost or PHEV support systems

communityRecommendations.content: Ask for the printed battery-test result and record whether the vehicle is Inline-6 or PHEV before accepting a replacement recommendation.
Do not assume a Group 35 upgrade or one Mazda part number fits both CX-70 powertrains; the factory test inputs are different.

before.title: CX-70 Low-Speed Clunk, Jerky Shift, or Hesitation - Diagnosis Required
before.description: Some 2025 CX-70 complaints describe a clunk, hesitation, shudder, or abrupt engagement during low-speed starts and shifts. Mazda's Large-platform eight-speed uses a mechanical launch clutch instead of a fluid torque converter and relies on precise clutch-hydraulic feedback control, but Mazda's design paper does not say harsh shifting is normal and the symptom alone does not identify a valve body, fluid, clutch, mount, driveline, hybrid-transition, or software fault. Warning lights or loss of drive power on an affected 2025 vehicle may instead fall under safety recall 24V-815.
before.solution: Record the speed, gear direction, temperature, state of charge, drive mode, throttle position, and whether the event occurs during engine/motor transition. Check the VIN for open recall 24V-815; if warning lights or loss of drive power occur, stop safely and have the free PCM/ECM recall remedy completed. For shift-quality complaints without that recall pattern, have the dealer reproduce the event, scan all powertrain modules before clearing codes, verify the installed calibration and adaptation data, and inspect fluid leaks, mounts, shafts, couplings, and transmission operation using Mazda service specifications. A valve body or fluid service should be selected only after testing identifies that repair and the dealer confirms the exact VIN-specific part and fluid requirement.
symptoms: Clunk or jerk during a low-speed shift
Hesitation when moving away from a stop
Abrupt engagement during engine and motor transition
Shudder during light-throttle maneuvering
Warning lights or loss of drive power in the recall pattern
affectedSystems: mechanical launch clutch and hydraulic control

communityRecommendations.content: Capture a short video of the cluster and note speed, drive mode, temperature, and battery state of charge so the same operating condition can be reproduced safely.
Do not buy a valve body or transmission fluid because a forum post uses the same symptom words; several software, hybrid, driveline, and mechanical causes can feel similar.

before.title: Blind Spot Monitoring (BSM) False/Phantom Rear-Corner Warnings
before.description: The rear-corner radar-based Blind Spot Monitoring system triggers false alerts, lighting up the mirror warning icons and/or sounding when no vehicle is present. Owners most commonly report this at highway speed, in rain or on wet roads (spray from other vehicles hitting the bumper-mounted sensors), in cold temperatures, and when driving between concrete jersey barriers or guardrails. Because the false alert suppresses the lane-change assist, drivers hesitate to change lanes. This is a separate radar system from the forward Smart Brake Support / i-Activsense camera, and is a distinct failure mode from phantom braking. NHTSA complaints for the 2025 CX-70 cite Safety Systems as one of the top problem areas.
before.solution: Dealers first inspect and clean the rear bumper radar sensors and check for bumper/paint work or aftermarket accessories that block them, then perform a radar recalibration and apply any available software update. Persistent cases are addressed with rear-corner radar sensor replacement. Many owners report inconsistent results and repeat visits; a definitive Mazda software remedy was still pending as of reporting. Interim workaround is toggling BSM off in poor conditions.
symptoms: Blind spot warning icon illuminates with nothing in the adjacent lane
False BSM chime when changing lanes
Warnings worse in rain, wet roads, or cold weather
Alerts trigger between jersey barriers/guardrails
Lane-change assist suppressed by phantom alert

proposal.title: Blind Spot Monitoring (BSM) False/Phantom Rear-Corner Warnings
proposal.description: Mazda TSB 15-001/26 applies to specified 2025-2026 CX-70 vehicles and documents a BSM warning that remains on while driving even though no vehicle is behind. Mazda identifies two possible contributors: electrical noise in the BSM control-module power supply and vibration or insufficient fastening at a rear side-radar mounting point. The bulletin does not limit the condition to rain, cold weather, barriers or sensor contamination, and it does not say that every false warning requires radar-module replacement.
proposal.solution: Have an authorised Mazda repairer verify the concern, confirm the VIN and installed BSM calibration, and perform the bulletin's ECU reprogramming. The bulletin also requires removal of the rear bumper to inspect the side-radar mounting condition; only an unacceptable mounting condition proceeds to the side-specific bracket, retainer and rivet repair followed by radar aiming. Do not buy a radar module or mounting hardware from this page; this is a VIN-, calibration- and side-specific dealer diagnosis with required calibration equipment.
symptoms: BSM warning remains on with no vehicle behind
False rear-corner warning while driving
One or both rear side-radar mounts require inspection

before.title: 2025 CX-70 Recall 7124J: Dash-ESU Startup Software Can Disable Safety Functions
before.description: Safety and emissions recall 7124J, NHTSA campaign 24V-814, covers certain 2025 CX-70 vehicles produced from December 5, 2023 through July 8, 2024. Improper Dash Electrical Supply Unit software can produce an error during startup, display multiple warnings, and prevent the windshield defroster, seat-belt warning, or 360-degree view monitor from working correctly. On PHEV vehicles, high-voltage battery cooling may also fail to operate as intended.

The recall remedy is a Dash-ESU reprogram with improved software at no charge; Mazda's notice estimates about half an hour for the repair, although the dealer may need the vehicle longer. This campaign does not call for buying or replacing the Dash-ESU. If warnings appear and a safety function is unavailable, follow the displayed warnings and arrange recall service rather than relying on that function.

Windshield defroster does not operate correctly

before.title: "Engine Malfunction – Have Engine Inspected" Warning from A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor Logic (DTC P0531 / TSB 07-001/25)
before.description: On PHEV models, an 'Engine Malfunction / Have Engine Inspected' message and check-engine light can appear at startup with DTC P0531:00 (A/C refrigerant pressure sensor No. 1 system, function malfunction) stored. Mazda TSB 07-001/25 (issued January 2025) identifies the root cause as improper control logic in the Powertrain Control Module (PCM) and Dash Electrical Supply Unit (Dash-ESU) misinterpreting the refrigerant pressure sensor signal — not an actual sensor or A/C hardware failure. It affects 2024-2025 CX-90 PHEV and 2025 CX-70 PHEV vehicles built before roughly mid-November 2024 (identified by VIN range). This is a distinct fault from the hybrid-system-stall warning; the vehicle typically still drives, but the warning is alarming and can be intermittent.
before.solution: Reprogram both the PCM and Dash-ESU with updated control-logic software using Mazda's M-MDS / MDARS per TSB 07-001/25 — free under warranty. Note: the initial software fix was temporarily suspended after it was found to break the MyMazda app remote climate control functions, so owners should confirm the dealer has the corrected patch before the reflash; interim guidance was to clear the DTC and wait for the updated software.
symptoms: 'Engine Malfunction – Have Engine Inspected' message at startup
Check engine light on
DTC P0531:00 stored
Intermittent recurrence after clearing
No stall but warning persists

before.title: Hybrid System Malfunction Warning with Engine Stall / Power Loss (PHEV)
before.description: CX-70 PHEV owners report a 'Hybrid System Malfunction' message in the instrument cluster accompanied by warning chimes, sometimes with related 'Electrical Leakage in Hybrid System Detected' or 'Charging System Malfunction' messages — including events that occur while charging at a home socket. On the shared platform these faults have been linked to power-control-module / battery-energy-control-module software that can interrupt hybrid-assist and cause the gasoline engine to stall or the vehicle to lose drive power. This is a drivability and safety concern given the risk of a stall or no-start.
before.solution: Have the dealer read the hybrid/high-voltage fault codes and apply all applicable power-control-module and battery-energy-control-module reprogramming plus any open recalls (the platform's inverter and hybrid-control software campaigns are directly relevant). Repeated leakage warnings warrant a high-voltage system insulation/leak inspection before returning the vehicle to service. Do not ignore the warning — reduce speed and get the vehicle inspected promptly. Diagnosis and reprogramming are covered under the hybrid/powertrain warranty; escalate to Mazda Corporate if a dealer cannot resolve a recurring warning.

proposal.title: Hybrid System Malfunction Warning with Engine Stall / Power Loss (PHEV)
proposal.description: The verified primary sources support several bounded 2025 CX-70 PHEV events, not one universal cause. Recall 24V-817 covers a small production population in which improper inverter software can activate fail-safe mode and limit motor power in EV mode. NHTSA complaint 11740990 records a Hybrid System Malfunction warning while driving, while complaint 11698488 records an owner-reported loss of motive power and shutdown after a prior recall update. Complaint narratives do not prove that the same component caused each event, and these sources do not establish the frozen 2026 scope.
proposal.solution: Treat a hybrid warning, shutdown or power loss as a safety concern. Move to a safe location when possible, preserve the warning and event details, check the VIN for open recalls, and have Mazda read all hybrid and high-voltage codes before clearing them. Recall 24V-817 has a free inverter-software remedy when applicable; a warning or power loss outside that exact campaign requires separate diagnosis rather than assuming the inverter, battery or charging system failed. Do not buy high-voltage parts from this page; all inspection and repair are VIN-, code- and campaign-specific dealer work.

before.title: Inaccurate Fuel Gauge Reading (Recall 78251)
before.description: Mazda recalled roughly 104,854 CX-70 and CX-90 vehicles because the instrument-cluster fuel gauge can display an inaccurate reading. When the tank is filled with ethanol-blended fuel, the ethanol can react with materials on the circuit board of the fuel-level sending unit, corrupting the reading. Owners can be misled into thinking they have more range than they do and run out of fuel without warning — a stall/loss-of-motive-power risk in traffic.
before.solution: This is a free safety recall (Mazda recall number 78251). Although the root cause is a chemical/material interaction, Mazda's fix is a software recalibration; because these vehicles do not support over-the-air updates, the vehicle must be taken to a dealer for the patch. Verify your VIN at mazdausa.com/owners/recalls or nhtsa.gov. Until repaired, refuel earlier than the gauge suggests. Mazda notified owners by mail through November 1, 2025.
symptoms: Fuel gauge shows more or less fuel than actual
Range estimate does not match fuel used
Vehicle runs low or empties unexpectedly
Erratic fuel-level needle movement

before.title: Water Intrusion into Cabin/Cargo Area (Liftgate Grommets, Sunroof/Roof-Rail Drains, A-Pillar)

before.title: Early 2025 CX-70 Liftgate Side-Spoiler Rattle on Rough Roads
before.description: Mazda documents a rattle or vibration from the liftgate area on specified early-production 2025 CX-70 vehicles when driving on rough roads. A gap at the attachment between a side-spoiler metal clip and the rear spoiler can let the parts vibrate. A noise heard from the rear cabin is easy to misidentify as suspension clunking, so stabilizer links, bushings, dampers, and mounts should not be condemned until the body and liftgate sources have been isolated.
before.solution: Reproduce the noise with the cargo area empty and record the road surface, speed, load, and whether light pressure on either rear side-spoiler area changes it. For an applicable VIN produced before January 7, 2025, Mazda's bulletin instructs the repairer to verify the affected side, remove that side spoiler, and install specified urethane and felt at the clip attachment before retesting. If the noise is clearly below the body or remains after the liftgate repair, inspect suspension fasteners, dampers, springs, control arms, bushings, stabilizer links, exhaust shields, and underbody panels for play, leakage, damage, or witness marks before selecting a replacement part.
symptoms: Rattle or vibration from the liftgate area on rough roads
Noise appears near one rear side-spoiler attachment
Rear-cabin noise can be mistaken for a suspension clunk
